pairs.source_text: Does grove_serve refuse a non-loopback bind?
pairs.source_norm: does grove_serve refuse a non-loopback bind?
pairs.target_text: No. run() prints a WARNING then calls uvicorn.run unconditionally. _host_looks_invalid rejects malformed values, not public ones. Verified 2026-08-30 on master.

pairs.source_text: What authenticates the Grove served page on 8766?
pairs.source_norm: what authenticates the grove served page on 8766?
pairs.target_text: Nothing. grep of grove_serve.py for authorization|bearer|token|cookie|api_key returns one hit, the word 'session' in an unrelated docstring. The loopback bind is the entire access control, and it is a default rather than a gate.

pairs.source_text: Does u2u bind a packet to its destination?
pairs.source_norm: does u2u bind a packet to its destination?
pairs.target_text: No. Packets carry to_addr (u2u/packets.py:46); u2u/dispatcher.py dispatch() reads only header.type and never reads to_addr. A signed packet addressed to a third party dispatches here. Verified 2026-08-30.

No. No nonce, seen-set, dedupe or packet id anywhere in u2u/*.py. The same packet six times dispatches six times. The two 'replay' mentions in source concern signature-error paths and consent-thread consumption, neither of which dedupes.

pairs.source_text: Does u2u filter inbound header keys?
pairs.source_norm: does u2u filter inbound header keys?
pairs.target_text: No. dispatch() passes the whole packet to the handler with no allowlist, so forged _denied or admin markers reach it. Signature verification upstream prevents forgery of a trusted peer, not replay, relay or attacker-added keys on their own signed packet.

pairs.source_text: Does the willows-grove repo have a v0.9.0 tag?
pairs.source_norm: does the willows-grove repo have a v0.9.0 tag?
pairs.target_text: Yes — on the remote at 2a15323, lightweight not annotated, so it carries no message and no Ratified-by. PyPI has exactly one release, 0.9.0. Earlier claims in pr14-carryovers and in PR #9's body that the repo had no tags were wrong; they came from git tag in a clone that had never fetched tags.

pairs.source_text: Did Grove start the way its operator guide documented?
pairs.source_norm: did grove start the way its operator guide documented?
pairs.target_text: No, not since v0.9. scripts/grove-serve-run, scripts/grove-watcher-run and the grove-serve/grove-watcher unit templates were referenced by docs/grove-served-page.md but never committed — lost in the v0.9 clean-build port. Restored and merged 2026-08-29; tests/test_documented_entrypoints_exist.py now pins doc-to-disk parity.
No. It was documented as the resident watcher's endpoint override but main() never read it — every run used the hardcoded default. Fixed 2026-08-29; the constructor already took the parameter.

pairs.source_text: How does the phone reach Grove?
pairs.source_norm: how does the phone reach grove?
pairs.target_text: It does not. Settled by Sean 2026-08-30: the phone is a removable volume that happens to compute — 'just another thumb drive'. No LAN path, no tunnel, no pairing, no discovery. 8766 stays loopback, D4 stays sealed, CLAUDE.md rule 1 holds. What must arrive at the box is the record, on plug-in.

pairs.source_text: What can the thumb-drive phone model not do?
pairs.source_norm: what can the thumb-drive phone model not do?
pairs.target_text: Push. Sneakernet cannot tap you on the shoulder: grove_human_required and every other alert waits until the phone is next plugged in. The archived remote-path-unification.md kept Discord alive for exactly this reason — it was the only path that notified a phone the human did not have open.

pairs.source_text: Is there an existing sneakernet sync primitive?
pairs.source_norm: is there an existing sneakernet sync primitive?
pairs.target_text: Candidate: nestor export / nestor import. Signed portable bundle (csv refused as lossy because it drops signatures), dry-run by default, --apply to write, --verifier names who accepted, conflicts and rejections surfaced by explicit flags. Not yet round-trip tested at 11k claims.

pairs.source_text: Where is the fleet's earlier phone design?
pairs.source_norm: where is the fleet's earlier phone design?
pairs.target_text: Two places. The networked shape is archived willow design/remote-path-unification.md — 318 lines, 2026-08-17, consolidating three remote paths behind one Pangolin-fronted MCP endpoint; it contains no vault, adb, offline or removable-media content and is superseded by the thumb-drive decision. The sneakernet shape is safe-app-store-public/apps/marching-arts/docs/BUILD_PLAN.md, reported by github-1b and not verified by me.

pairs.source_text: Does the fleet already handle removable media?
pairs.source_norm: does the fleet already handle removable media?
pairs.target_text: Yes. willow-2.0 willow/fylgja/config/kart-sandbox.json:105 binds /run/media into the Kart sandbox (#302), and docs/recovery/willow-sandbox-2026-04-skeleton records a clone recovered from USB drive SEAN. The sync stage reads a mounted volume through machinery that already exists; the build stage does not — kart-sandbox.json names android/gradle/sdk zero times.

willow-2.0 apps/ratatosk — two-ended local-first console, phone (Termux) and desktop, with a versioned envelope protocol shared by both ends, a capability-gated desktop listener, doctor.py, and termux/ carrying boot, install.sh, shortcuts and ui. Tailnet-first by default: the transport is wrong for the thumb-drive model, the shape is right.

pairs.source_text: Is willows-grove in the Nestor corpus?
pairs.source_norm: is willows-grove in the nestor corpus?
pairs.target_text: No — zero claims as of 2026-08-30 per github-1b, unverified by me. Every finding in this bundle was therefore invisible to the corpus at the time it was made.
